brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean typographic hierarchy with confident percentage display anchoring each card and tidy uppercase metric labels
Restrained dark palette with single green accent feels calm and monitoring-appropriate without visual noise
Symmetric two-card layout reads instantly; metric chips below rings provide clear secondary detail
dominant_weaknesses: Brief promised organism metaphor — breathing/pulsing motion — but static screenshot shows identical green rings, no living differentiation
Both CPU and Memory use the same green despite 'Moderate · Pulse elevated' text suggesting stress; color should diverge to encode state
Vast empty lower halves of cards waste canvas; rings float without environmental context like waveform, breath line, or history
fix_priorities: Encode organism state in color and motion: green steady breath vs amber/red faster pulse, with visible rhythm even in stills
Add a subtle breathing waveform or pulse trail in the empty card space to reify the metaphor
Differentiate the two rings visually so 'Healthy' and 'Moderate' are pre-attentively distinct, not just text-labeled
Tighten card height or add a third metric row to reduce dead vertical space
rationale.norman_balance: Decent visceral polish and adequate behavioral clarity, but reflective payoff is thin because the organism concept never manifests beyond labels.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the copy nods to the metaphor but the visual system shows two identical dashboards, failing to make CPU and memory feel like distinct living things.
